wikiGoal:
A knowledge wiki for the OpenVerifiers repository: the design history, the
reasoning-engine architecture, and the research that informs open design
questions.

This wiki is a project wiki, not a pure code wiki: it documents intent,
decisions, and open questions. Sources of truth:

- `docs/design.md` — canonical design history (finalized v1 decisions).
- `docs/newer-additions.md` — newer design additions, each marked
  finalized-v1 / out-of-scope-v1 / open-research.
- `docs/research/` — research briefs (01–06) + `synthesis.md` (decision
  recommendations and conflict flags).
- `ARCHITECTURE.md` — implementation spec of the built engine.
- The Python SDK under `openverifiers/` (package) and `tests/`.
- `RESULTS.md` — physics benchmark record.

Page conventions: every page that states a decision or an open question must
mark it with one of: `[v1]` finalized v1 scope, `[out-v1]` explicitly out of
scope for v1, `[open]` open research feeding a not-yet-finalized decision.
Ground claims in the sources above with repo:// or docs:// references. Never
invent numbers, systems, or citations. Where research findings conflict with a
prior decision, say so explicitly on the page and link the conflict to
`docs/research/synthesis.md`.

pages.title: Core Ontology — Facts, Transformations, Unknowns
pages.purpose: Documents the three node kinds (Fact, Transformation, Unknown) as implemented in model.py and specified in ARCHITECTURE.md §1: fact identity/dedup, statuses, transformation precondition/relation/solver_hook, and first-class Unknown.
instructions: Cross-link to engine.md (how the ontology is searched) and unknown-open-world.md (the Unknown semantics).
Existing page; keep the [v1] decision markers and repo:// references to model.py and ARCHITECTURE.md §1.

pages.title: Reasoning Engine — Deduction and Induction
pages.purpose: Documents engine.py: backward deduction as goal refinement with a visiting-set loop guard and per-kind memoization (deduce), forward induction as fixed-point closure with ancestor-guard and id-dedup (induce), the DAG-by-construction invariants, trace events recorded, and RESOLVED vs UNKNOWN verdict paths.
instructions: Emphasize the DAG/no-loops invariant as a correctness and explainability guarantee, not a performance shortcut.
Existing page; keep repo:// references to engine.py and ARCHITECTURE.md §2-§3.

pages.title: Packaging Layers — SDK, CLI, MCP
pages.purpose: Documents the strict three-layer boundary: SDK core (public surface in __init__.py, verify_physics domain driver), thin CLI (cli.py calls only the SDK), and the designed-but-not-built MCP server and statistical pipeline; plus the future domain-adapter rule that domain code lives in grammars/ only.
instructions: Distinguish implemented behavior from spec-only MCP/statistical layers explicitly.
Existing page; keep repo:// references to __init__.py, cli.py and ARCHITECTURE.md §7.

pages.title: Physics Vertical Slice — Grammar and Extraction
pages.purpose: Documents the physics domain implementation: KIND_META fact kinds with dimensions/units, the rule library in grammars/physics.py (kinematics, dynamics, energy transformations), the dimension-enforcing rule precondition, and the deterministic regex schema-forced extraction in grammars/input.py with explicit overrides and target detection.
instructions: Document the deterministic (non-LLM) extraction scope and the explicit-override mechanism for register the regexes miss.
Mark the physics grammar as the [v1] manual-grammar slice and note auto-extraction is [out-v1]/benchmark-gated.

pages.title: Solver Hooks and Dimension Checking
pages.purpose: Documents solvers.py: dimensions as {L,M,T} exponent dicts with dim_add/dim_sub/dim_eq checked by rule preconditions, the SOLVERS registry with get_solver dispatch, and the sympy.algebra backend (solve_symbolic) with its failure contract and positive-root magnitude convention for velocity-like targets.
instructions: Existing page; keep repo:// references to solvers.py and note the 'core never imports sympy directly' boundary.

pages.title: Trace Store and Render Views
pages.purpose: Documents the one-verbose-store trace policy: the engine appends every derive/reject/deadend/join/unknown event to a single store, and trace.py's build_views projects success-path, failure-trail, and full views from it; render_view formats them.
instructions: Existing page; keep repo:// references to trace.py and ARCHITECTURE.md §4.
Note the open question on trace-storage scaling (ARCHITECTURE.md §9 item 1) as [open].

pages.title: First-Class Unknown and Open-World Semantics
pages.purpose: Documents the Unknown node as a legitimate auditable outcome (not a failure), its Open-World-Assumption semantics grounded in DL research, the verified/contradicted/unverified-unknown verdict vocabulary, and the CONFLICT between this and users' closed-world intuition.
instructions: Distinguish RESOLVED-UNKNOWN ('cannot yet be proven') from a hard fail ('proven wrong') as [v1].
Mark the first-class Unknown as [v1] and flag the open-world-vs-closed-world intuition CONFLICT, linking to docs/research/synthesis.md.

pages.title: Dual Pipeline — Symbolic and Statistical
pages.purpose: Captures the README/design dual-pipeline concept: deterministic solver-backed symbolic verification plus LLM-as-judge statistical verification for non-formalizable claims; documents the decision that only the symbolic core is implemented in v1 and the statistical/LLM-judge layer is a spec-shaped stub.
instructions: Ground the confidence-scored verdict shape (retained in CLI output) in README/ARCHITECTURE §10.
Mark the statistical pipeline as [out-v1]/not-built and the sequencing decision (prove the deterministic core first) as [v1].

pages.title: Physics Benchmark — Problem Set and Runner
pages.purpose: Documents the physics benchmark: tests/problems.py (20 JEE/CBSE/HSC problems with expected answers and explicit overrides), tests/run_benchmark.py (pass criteria, RESULTS.md generation), and the current 20/20 results.
instructions: Document the pass criterion (status RESOLVED within 1e-6 relative tolerance) and that a UNKNOWN verdict counts as a fail in this benchmark.
Ground the 20/20 result exactly in RESULTS.md; do not invent other numbers.

pages.title: Running OpenVerifiers — CLI, MCP, and CI
pages.purpose: Documents operational usage: invoking the CLI with --view/--explicit/--target/--json, the benchmark runner command, the spec-shaped MCP serve entrypoint, and the scheduled OpenWiki GitHub Actions update workflow (openwiki-update.yml).
instructions: Document the OpenWiki CI workflow that regenerates openwiki/ pages; generated pages are not hand-edited.
Ground CLI flags in cli.py and note the MCP serve path is a spec/designed entrypoint [out-v1], with the boundary rule that domain logic stays out of the CLI/MCP layer.

pages.title: Composition, Loose Relationships, and OWNER Context
pages.purpose: Documents design additions #1/#2/#3: typed node composition via slot descriptors (frames), open/loose typed relationships, and the OWNER/reference-frame context problem solved by the value-object (n-ary) pattern importing shapes from RDF-star, with the requirement that context renders in the trace.
instructions: Link the default_candidate-never-truth and refusal-on-inheritance-conflict resolutions to docs/research/synthesis.md.
Mark typed composition, loose relationships, and OWNER as [v1] directions; note property graphs are a storage substrate, not semantic authority.

pages.title: Correlation Chains, Path Analysis, and the Guardrail
pages.purpose: Documents design addition #4/#5: the flagged risk of silently multiplying correlation coefficients as exact proportionalities, the path-analysis/SEM and Bayesian-network formalisms that correct it, and the recommended chain-composition guardrail that refuses with a diagnostic Unknown unless edges are causal with error terms.
instructions: Mark the guardrail as [open]→recommended (not yet implemented) and the first-class uncertainty direction as [v1].
State the CONFLICT that correlation is not transitive and link to docs/research/synthesis.md; the default is refusal-with-Unknown, never a silently computed number.

pages.title: Research Synthesis and Conflict Flags
pages.purpose: Routes the six research briefs and records the decision bridge: what prior art validates (TBox/ABox, OWA, DAG, transformation-as-relation), the flagged correlation-chain risk, and the decision-record table with updated statuses and each CONFLICT flagged to docs/research/synthesis.md.
instructions: Mark each research addition's status as finalized-v1 / out-of-scope-v1 / open-research per the synthesis decision record.
Preserve every CONFLICT flag and cite docs/research/synthesis.md for resolutions.

pages.title: Structural Layer — DL ABox/TBox Discipline
pages.purpose: Documents design addition #9 and its deepening: the two content sources map to the DL TBox/ABox split, a DL reasoner as an optional oracle for global consistency, the profile-choice-and-expressivity tradeoff, and the sameAs/differentFrom identity policy needed before DL checking is trustworthy.
instructions: Flag the DL+arithmetic undecidability conflict and the profile-choice product decision from docs/research/synthesis.md.
Mark the TBox/ABox naming and two-content-source separation as [v1], and the DL-reasoner oracle as [open]/optional, out-of-scope for the v1 code path.

pages.title: End-to-End Verify Workflow
pages.purpose: Traces the runtime control and data flow of a verify() run across system boundaries — CLI/SDK entry, schema-forced extraction to unverified_truth facts, engine.deduce backward chaining, dimension-checked rule firing via the sympy solver, trace recording, and view projection to a VerificationResult — with a mermaid runtime diagram.
instructions: Include the no-target UNKNOWN short-circuit and the RESOLVED vs UNKNOWN verdict paths as [v1] behavior.
Use a mermaid diagram (see /skills/mermaid-diagrams/SKILL.md) to show the call sequence and data flow.

pages.title: OpenVerifiers Wiki — Quickstart and Routing Map
pages.purpose: Entry point that routes readers through the whole wiki hierarchy: the architecture (built engine), the design concepts, the research decisions, the end-to-end verify workflow, and the benchmark/operations. Explains the page convention markers [v1]/[out-v1]/[open], the sources of truth, and the hierarchy index.
instructions: Mark every decision or open question with [v1], [out-v1], or [open] and ground claims with repo:// or docs:// references.
Route readers through the hierarchy (architecture, concepts, research, workflows, operations) rather than flattening them into a page list.
